## The live site is current — measured, not assumed

Both audits reviewed `detailingplatform.com`. The repo's old notes claimed live
was hundreds of commits behind, which would have made most findings stale.
**It is not.** On 2026-09-16 the live bundle and a fresh local build from `HEAD`
were byte-identical:

```
live:  assets/index-CfUTS91_.js   assets/index-DrofU7fn.css
local: assets/index-CfUTS91_.js   assets/index-DrofU7fn.css
```

**So every finding below is against current code and none of it is discounted.**
It also means a push to `main` publishes. Re-measure with the two commands in
CLAUDE.md § Publishing rather than trusting this paragraph later.

## How to work this queue

**`docs/BATCHES.md` is the running order — start there, not here.** This file
is 9,000 lines ordered by risk, which makes it a queue rather than a plan for
one sitting. `BATCHES.md` groups the open items into session-sized batches,
marks each one lane **A** (touches `app/src`) or **B** (does not) so two
sessions can run without colliding, and names the model each batch deserves.
It re-orders nothing here and duplicates nothing here. **This file stays the
source of truth for what an item is and why.**

1. **One item at a time, top to bottom.** Waves are ordered by what costs money
   or trust first. Don't batch.
2. **Fix, don't rebuild.** Only touch a screen for a problem named here.
3. **Verify in a real browser before ticking.** Try the case that should work
   *and* the case that should be refused. Check 1440 wide and 375 wide.
   A code change alone is not a fix.
4. **Tick the box and add one line saying how you checked it.** That line is
   what stops the next session re-doing it.
5. **When a finding turns out to be wrong, say so and strike it** — don't
   silently drop it. § Watch list below has the ones already suspect.
6. **Grep every caller before fixing.** A1's P0-02 was reported on one page and
   is actually on two; the one-guard fix covers both. Assume the same of
   anything that looks like a one-off.

- [ ] **0.11 — Move photo storage to Cloudflare R2.** Buckets already exist and
  already match the code names. **The allowance goes from 1 GB to 10 GB IN THE
  SAME CHANGE as the upload switch, never a commit earlier**, so the screen
  never promises storage that does not exist. **And the move loses the
  database-enforced tenant isolation** — R2 has no equivalent of the
  `foldername` policy, so that guard is rebuilt in our own code and has to be
  right before one real photo is written. Design, arithmetic and the two ways
  the cap fails silently: `docs/the-photo-allowance.md`.
  ---

  #### THE GUARD R2 DOES NOT HAVE IS WRITTEN — 2026-09-24. Nothing else moved.

  **`supabase/functions/_shared/photoKey.ts`, with
  `tests/photo-key-isolation.test.mjs`. 61 assertions, credential-free, no dev
  server.**

  **WHAT IT REPLACES.** Postgres keeps one detailer out of another's photographs
  with `(storage.foldername(name))[1] in (select public.current_business_ids()::text)`
  on `storage.objects` — `20260906010000_job_photos.sql`, and the same shape on
  `expense-receipts` and `business-media`. **R2 has no equivalent, because it has
  no idea what a business is.** The move does not merely change where bytes live:
  **it deletes a guard the database has enforced since 2026-08-27.** This is the
  first of `docs/the-photo-allowance.md` § 4's *"two questions at that door"*:
  **is this your business?** The second — *do you have room?* — is
  `job_photo_budget()` and **is not built here.**

  **AN ALLOWLIST, NOT A DENYLIST, and that is the whole design.** The two obvious
  implementations are wrong:

  ```js
  key.split("/")[0] === businessId      // WRONG
  key.startsWith(businessId + "/")      // WRONG
  ```

  **Both answer yes to `B/../A/booking/photo.jpg`**, whose first segment is `B` and
  whose object is `A`'s. Every denylist for that — strip `..`, reject `%2f`,
  normalise backslashes — is a list somebody has to keep complete, and its failure
  is silent: the guard still returns `true`, nothing goes red, and the cross-tenant
  checks pass on the day it is written.

  **So nothing is stripped or normalised. A key is parsed against the ONE shape
  `storagePath()` mints — `businessId/ownerId/id.ext`, three canonical lowercase
  uuids — anchored at both ends, and anything else is not a key.** `..` is not a
  uuid. `%2f` is not hex. A leading slash makes the first segment empty. **The
  attack surface is not defended against; it is unrepresentable.**

  **THE TEST CALLS THE MINTER RATHER THAN DESCRIBING IT.** It imports
  `storagePath()` from `app/src/lib/photo-rules.js` and feeds its output to the
  guard, so *"the guard accepts what we store"* is proved by running both. **Two
  copies of a path rule that can disagree is this repo's most repeated failure**,
  and the minter's own header warns about precisely that for its half.

  **STRICTNESS WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED.** A guard this narrow would refuse any
  object stored under an older shape. Read against the live database (read-only,
  `kguqylyzgyzfktkfnhjb`, confirmed before the query): **`job_photos` holds 0 rows,
  0 bytes, 0 distinct paths**, and **no expense carries a receipt path.** There is
  no legacy key to honour. **If that ever stops being true this file must be
  widened deliberately, not loosened to make a run go green.**

  **WHAT THE CHECK ASKS:** 4 minted keys through every `extForType` branch; **17
  wrong-tenant keys** — A's own key handed to B, four traversal shapes, a
  percent-encoded separator, backslashes, a leading slash, a bucket name glued on
  the front, an absolute URL, a query string smuggling the other tenant, a null
  byte, an uppercase uuid, a trailing space, a bare prefix, a wildcard, the empty
  string; **10 bad callers** — `undefined`, `null`, `""`, `"*"`, a prefix of the
  id, an array, an object, a trailing slash, an uppercased id, a SQL fragment; the
  refusal message asserted to name **neither** the key nor the other tenant,
  because a refusal that echoes it tells a prober the object exists and whose it
  is; and **both naive guards run and asserted to be fooled** by the key the real
  one refuses.

  **BROKEN ON PURPOSE THREE WAYS:** the naive split swapped in — **5 red**,
  including the assertion written to catch exactly that; **always-yes — 22 red**;
  **always-no — 5 red**. Restored, **61/61**. A guard that cannot refuse and a
  guard that refuses everything are both caught, in opposite directions, by
  assertions that exist on every run.

  **EXPLICITLY NOT DONE, and each is deliberate:**
  * **no upload path switched** — no presigned-URL function, no R2 client, no
    bucket call;
  * **`photo_total_gb` untouched at 1.** It goes to 10 **in the same change as the
    switch, never a commit earlier** — `docs/the-photo-allowance.md` § 2 — and that
    change is in `app/src`, which was another session's;
  * **no photo written**, and `job_photos` still holds 0 rows;
  * **no key read or printed.** Where the R2 credentials live is
    `docs/services-and-secrets.md`; their values were never queried, in full or as
    a prefix;
  * the **budget** half of the door, and the **periodic reconcile** of § 6 —
    `businessPrefix()` exists for the reconcile to sum against, and the reconcile
    itself is not written.

  **So 0.11's box stays `[ ]`.** The dangerous half is done and proved; the switch
  is the rest of the item.

  **Done when** (written 2026-09-25; this item had none): uploads go to R2 through
  the presigned-URL door and nowhere else; **`photo_total_gb` is 10 in that same
  change and not a commit earlier**; the door refuses a key belonging to another
  business (already guarded — `tests/photo-key-isolation.test.mjs`) **and** refuses
  over the cap with a message naming what is used, what the limit is and that
  deleting old job photos frees it; each `job_photos` row's `bytes` equals **the
  size R2 reports for the stored object**, not the size the client claimed; and the
  reconcile of `docs/the-photo-allowance.md` § 6 exists, reports drift **as a
  number**, and **runs from a cron entry the way `refresh-weather` does** — named
  that way rather than "on a schedule", corrected 2026-09-25, because a stranger
  cannot check "on a schedule" without being told where schedules live.
  **What failing looks like — both shapes are named in that document and neither
  shows up as an error:** `job_photos.bytes` stopping landing, so the cap is
  compared against zero and **silently becomes unlimited**, surfacing as a bill
  rather than a failure; and the recorded size being the client's claim, so a
  browser that under-reports buys itself unlimited storage.

  ***PREPARED 2026-10-06 (Lane A and the server half, in a scratch folder), NOTHING APPLIED, NOTHING COMMITTED BUT THIS NOTE,
  NOTHING DEPLOYED. The box stays `[ ]`.*** The item is carved into slices; the first three and a bug found on the way are
  written as five patches that each pass `git apply --check` against HEAD `a84fd72` and apply together in either order:
  1. **`photo-door-slice1.patch`, the app half for job photos** (9 files: `photo-door.js` new, `photos.js`, `api.js`,
     `Gallery.jsx`, `JobPhotos.jsx`, `appEs.js`, and three tests). The contract is the header of `app/src/lib/photo-door.js`:
     four actions on `photo-door` (`start`, `finish`, `urls`, `remove`). It fails in words until the server half exists and has
     **no fallback to Supabase Storage**, on purpose.
  2. **`photo-door-server.patch`, slice 2, the door itself** (6 files: `photo-door/index.ts`, `_shared/photoDoor.ts` and
     `_shared/r2.ts` new, a ceiling in `rateLimit.ts`, two tests). **Credentials are read from the environment by name only**
     (`R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`) and never reach a log, an answer or a URL.
  3. **`photo-door-forget.patch`, slice 3** (4 files): `delete-customer` now removes a forgotten customer's photo files from
     **both** stores, R2 and Supabase Storage, and counts a file only once each store confirms it is gone. `job_photos.path` is
     the same string in both and the row does not say which, so removing from one would have left a stranger's car in the other
     while reporting success. A key of another business, R2 not configured while photos exist, and any store failing all stop
     everything before the rows are deleted.
  4. **`siteintake-photos.patch`** (2 files): `SiteIntake.jsx` called `addPhoto({ ..., kind: "gallery" })` with no booking. That
     function files a job photo, so `storagePath` throws without a booking and `job_photos.kind` only allows before, after or
     damage: it cannot have worked since commit `3b97ed0`. It now sends the photos to `business-media` under `intake/` and
     publishes nothing. The new `tests/photo-call-sites.test.mjs` reads every `addPhoto(` call in `app/src` and would have

  5. **`no-show-way-back.patch`** (4.1 ruling 3) is a separate item and is listed only because it shares `appEs.js`.
  **Proved, in a scratch copy of the repo at that HEAD with all five applied, no network and no database:** the 13 suites named in

  **Two faults the runs found and the patches already carry the fix for:** `job_photo_budget()` guards itself with
  `current_business_ids()`, which reads the CALLER's session, so asked with the service-role key it returns **no rows**, and a door

  **NOT PROVEN, SAID PLAINLY:** that R2 accepts these signatures (the first real upload after publishing is that proof); anything

  **FOR ANDREW, at publish:** (a) a CORS rule on the `job-photos` bucket in Cloudflare allowing the app's web address (and

  lawyers rather than from scratch, and fix the promises so they match the
  product. The live pages' real problem is not that a lawyer has not blessed
  them — it is that they **contradict the pricing page** (7.7) and **omit data
  processors the product actually uses** (7.8). Both of those are factual bugs
  we can fix for nothing.

  before charging strangers at scale. A business entity still matters more than
  the review — right now the terms are a contract with a private individual.
  *Sources: [Promise Legal SaaS ToS template](https://promise.legal/templates/terms-of-service), [ToS Lawyer's US SaaS legal checklist](https://toslawyer.com/legal-checklist-for-u-s-saas-startups-tos-privacy-dpa-sla-and-more/).*

  clauses, it is one sentence.**

  > customers' information, and six more do.** A customer's name travels in
  > the body of a push notification and their typed address goes to an
  > address-lookup service, and nobody reading that page would know it.

  person would care about**, and it is exactly the class of defect this item
  was written for. It was found by listing every external host the edge

  perfectly well and is false.

  **WHAT ACTUALLY RECEIVES DATA, beyond the five the page named.** A customer's
  typed address goes to **Geoapify** while they are typing it. The
  **coordinates of the job address** go to the **US National Weather Service**,

  **DeepL** or to **Google's translation service**, a second Google service
  where the page names Google only for sign-in. And the owner's phone alerts
  carry **the customer's name in the notification body**, which travels through
  **whichever push service the detailer's browser uses** — Google's, Mozilla's
  or Apple's. `api.deepl.com` never showed up in a source scan because the
  host is built from the API key.

## Wave 2 — Booking truth

A customer must never be shown one price and charged another, never be handed
the wrong service, and never book a job we cannot reach.

- [ ] **2.1 — The total rises after the customer has picked the time.**
  **THE FIX IS WRITTEN AND IT IS NOT LIVE (measured 2026-10-06). Nothing a
  customer sees has changed. The only thing standing between here and a
  customer being shown the right price is Andrew pressing publish on
  `calculate-booking`.**

  **RE-MEASURED 2026-10-06 AND IT STILL HOLDS — PRESSED, NOT READ.** The
  deployed `calculate-booking`, asked for `demo-detail`'s Express Wash on
  Saturday 2026-10-10 **with a date and no time**, returned `adjustments: []` and
  a total of **$80**. Asked with the date **and** `start_time: "10:00"`, the same
  function returned `Weekend rate +30` and **$110**. So the day surcharge is
  live when a time is present and absent when only the day is — which is exactly
  the fault, and the fix (a day-only `whenContextFor` branch) is not in the
  running copy. Command: a POST to `/functions/v1/calculate-booking` with the
  two bodies above; `node scripts/deployed-inventory.mjs` also lists the function
  among those differing from the checkout.

  **What a customer sees TODAY.** They choose Saturday the 26th or Sunday the
  27th, the page lists the times available that day, and the running total
  says **$65**. Nothing anywhere on the screen mentions a weekend, a surcharge
  or thirty dollars. They pick a time and the total becomes **$95**. Walked
  fresh in a real browser on 2026-09-22 by Andrew, after the fix was written
  and committed, on both days. **This is still what happens.**

  **What a customer will see AFTER `calculate-booking` is published.** They
  choose the same Saturday, and the total says **$95** straight away, with the
  words **`Weekend rate · +$30`** on the screen above the list of times. The
  price does not move again when they pick a time. A weekday is unaffected and
  stays at $65 throughout.

  **Why it is not live (as of 2026-10-06), in one sentence:** the sum is worked out by a program
  that runs on Supabase rather than in the browser, and that program has to be
  published to start running the new version.

  **REFRAMED 2026-09-24 ON ANDREW'S RULING — this is a DEFERRAL, not a blocker.**
  The fix is **done and correct on disk and switched off until launch.** He does
  not care about the live site because nothing is using it, so the publish is
  **the switch**, not a gate he is failing to open. `DECISIONS.md` § *"Publishing
  is a DEFERRAL, not a blocker"*. **Still true and still worth knowing:**
  `deployed-inventory.mjs` reports these functions as differing, and on launch
  day that is the difference between shipping this fix and shipping the old
  number.

  **How anyone will know it worked:** `node scripts/surcharge-visible.mjs`
  goes from 40 failures to zero. It is red today on purpose.

  **RE-MEASURED 2026-09-23 AND THE BLOCKER IS REAL, NOT STALE.** 2.8's blocker
  turned out to have expired on the 21st; this one has not, and the difference
  is the whole reason somebody had to go and look.

  **THE BLOCKER WAS MEASURED AGAIN ON 2026-09-23, BECAUSE A STALE BLOCKER AND
  A REAL ONE LOOK IDENTICAL FROM THE ROADMAP.** Both 2.1 and 2.8 said the same
  sentence — *the fix is written, it is not live, only a publish is left* — and
  only one of them was still true. The bundles were fetched from the Management
  API with the `.env` token and counted the way 2.8's own 2026-09-21 table
  counted them, so the numbers sit beside the old ones:

  | Deployed bundle | 2026-09-21 said | 2026-09-23 says |
  |---|---|---|
  | `create-booking` v84 | `address_source` **x0** | `body.address_source==="picked"` **x1**, `addressSource:booking.address_source` **x2** |
  | `get-booking-receipt` v61 | `address_source` **x0** | `"address_source"` in its column list **x1** |
  | `send-owner-reminders` v79 | `address_source` **x0** | `addressSource:` **x2** |
  | `calculate-booking` v61 | — | day-only `whenContextFor` return **x0** |

  **COUNTED WITH CODE-ONLY TOKENS, AFTER A COMMENT NEARLY FOOLED THE FIRST
  ATTEMPT.** `deployed-inventory.mjs`'s own method is comment-text comparison,
  so **comments survive into the bundle** — and the first probe counted
  `!bookingDate||!startTime`, which appears in the CHECKOUT once, inside the

  checkout is what caught it. The discriminating token is
  `if(!startTime)return{weekday:weekdayOf(bookingDate)}`, which exists in the

  **THE DEPLOYED `calculate-booking` v61 CARRIES THE DAY-ONLY RETURN ZERO
  TIMES.** So the server still refuses to price a day without an hour, exactly
  as before, and the page — which does carry its half — has nothing to draw.

  **PRESSED, NOT INFERRED, at the two widths the walk asks for.** Saturday 26

  | Width | With the day chosen | After a time is tapped |
  |---|---|---|
  | 392x844 | **$65**, nothing naming a weekend | $95 · `Weekend rate · +$30` |
  | 320x844 | **$65**, nothing naming a weekend | $95 · `Weekend rate · +$30` |

  **BUILDING IT FOUND THREE FAULTS IN ITSELF BEFORE IT FOUND NONE IN THE
  PRODUCT, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH READING.**
  1. **It raced the network and reported a product defect.** `settle()` ends
     when the DOM has been quiet for 130ms, and between a chip tap and
     `calculate-booking`'s answer the DOM is perfectly quiet — so one target
     in ten printed *"no surcharge line was rendered at all"*. A stopwatch
     fault wearing a pricing fault's clothes. The first repair,
     `Promise.race([answer, wait(2500)])`, reads like a wait and behaves like
     a deadline; it failed once in fifteen, which is the frequency that gets
     written off as flaky. The page now counts its own quote requests.
  2. **THE CANARY CAUGHT 0 OF 5 OVER A DEFECT THAT WAS PLAINLY IN ITS OWN
     SCREENSHOT.** The canary puts the note back below the chips — the exact
     layout that shipped 09-13 to 09-21 — and it kept passing. The cause was
     this script's own gate probe: roadmap 2.6 says a refused press turns the
     reason on AND SCROLLS TO IT, so pressing Continue early left the page at
     the bottom of a 1,400px step, and everything measured afterwards was
     measured from a position the script itself created. **A check whose act
     of looking moves the thing it is looking at** — the same shape as the
     `git diff --cached` correction in CLAUDE.md. Scroll reset to the top
     after the probe; the canary now catches **5 of 5**, at y=1074 against a
     bar at 771.
  3. **THE PIXEL TEST LET A BLANKED LINE THROUGH AT 392.** The first version
     measured the standard deviation of luminance inside the line's rect;
     `--break=paint` caught nine targets and scored **3.49 against a floor of
     4** on the tenth, because the rect sits on this page's gradient and the
     spread is mostly BACKGROUND. Replaced with the difference between two
     renders of the same frame — `pinned-bar.mjs`'s `edge` correction, made a
     second time in a second file. Real text moves its rect by 4.4 levels at
     the desk widths and 8.9–9.1 at 320; a blanked one by **0.00 at all ten**.

  functions are behind this checkout, `calculate-booking` among them, by 1.3
  days — but that gap is 14.9's rate-limit work awaiting Andrew's publish and
  does not touch pricing.** The walk above went through the REAL deployed
  function, not an injected response, which is the difference between this

  **UNTICKED THE SAME EVENING. ANDREW REPRODUCED THE WALK ABOVE, THEN DID THE
  ONE THING IT DOES NOT DO, AND THE ITEM WAS STILL TRUE.** He picked a
  different open weekend day — Sunday the 27th — and simply waited three and a
  half seconds without touching a time. `HORARIOS DEL DOMINGO, 27 DE
  SEPTIEMBRE`. Nine time buttons. `Total estimado · 1 h · $65`. He searched the
  whole rendered text for "Weekend rate", for "+$30" and for "recargo":
  **none of them present.** Not below the fold, not late-rendering, not there.

  **THE LABEL I MEASURED IS REAL, AND IT APPEARS IN THE SAME RENDER AS THE
  PRICE CHANGE. The disclosure does not precede the charge; it arrives with
  it.** That is this item's own sentence, word for word, and it was still true
  after the item was ticked.

  **WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE THIRTY DOLLARS.** The surcharge is a function
  of the DAY. Read off the tenant's own `business_settings` rather than off
  `MANAGER-CLOSE` — which had already handed out one wrong number that day:
  `label: "Weekend rate"`, `kind: "time"`, `weekdays: [0, 6]`,
  **`start_time: null`, `end_time: null`** — no hour anywhere in it. So the
  product KNOWS the price is $95 the instant the customer taps Sunday, and
  goes on showing $65 while they browse nine times. Not a limitation. **A
  disclosure late by one step for no reason, on the one screen that takes
  money.**

  **AND THE LESSON IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX.** `surcharge-visible.mjs` was
  built to answer *"is the surcharge visible"* and answered **yes, correctly**,
  at fifteen targets. The question that needed asking was *"is it visible
  BEFORE the customer can be charged it"*. **One word apart, opposite
  answers.** A walk that goes day, then time, then look can never see the gap,
  **because the gap closes on the tap that ends it.** The only state in which
  the fault exists is the one between the two taps, and the check walked
  straight through it. Written up in `docs/gotchas.md` with its two siblings
  from the same day.

  **THE CHECK WAS MADE TO GO RED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS FIXED, AND COMMITTED IN
  THAT STATE ON PURPOSE — `154742f`** — because a check that has only ever run
  against fixed code has never proved it can see the bug. Four new assertions
  per weekend target, asked of the state between the taps: `early-named`,
  `early-priced`, `early-visible`, `early-painted`.

  | Run, before any fix | Result |
  |---|---|
  | The four `early-*`, ten weekend targets | **FAIL — 40 failures**, at 1920, 1440x900, 768x1024, 392x844 and 320 |
  | The five after-time assertions | green — the first round's work still holds |
  | **Weekday control, five widths** | **green**, `$65 → $65 → $65`, so the check is not simply always-red |
  | Canary "order" / canary "stripped" | 5/5 and 5/5 |

  **A SECOND CANARY FLAVOUR WAS ADDED AND IT IS THE INTERESTING ONE.** The old
  canary puts the note back below the chips, which proves the check can see a
  line in the wrong PLACE. **Nothing proved it could see a line that is not
  there at all** — so `named` had never once been observed failing, and an
  assertion that has never failed is an assertion nobody has tested.
  `stripped` removes `adjustments` from the server's answer on the way past.
  Both flavours, five runs each, catch every time.

  **THE FIX IS TWO HALVES AND NEITHER IS SUFFICIENT.**
  1. **Server — `_shared/pricing.ts`.** `whenContextFor` opened with
     `if (!bookingDate || !startTime) return {}`. It now returns
     `{ weekday }` when a day is known and an hour is not. **This is not a
     loosening:** `matchPriceRules` demands a `startTime` only INSIDE the
     branch for a rule carrying a start AND an end time, and refuses a
     `lead_time` rule whenever `leadHours` is null, so every rule that
     genuinely needs the hour still correctly declines.
  2. **Page — `StepWhen.jsx`.** The note was gated on `legTime`, so even a
     priced day would have stayed silent. The surcharge lines now render on
     the DAY; the request-mode sentence keeps its `legTime`, because it says
     "once this TIME is accepted" and there is no time yet. **One condition
     changed, no new copy, no new mechanism, no CSS** — the named fault was
     the timing of one label and one number, and the fix is that size.

  **THE SERVER HALF IS PROVED BY `tests/price-a-day.test.mjs`** — eight tests
  against the real module with the tenant's real rules, plus an invented
  windowed "Evening rate" that must keep declining. **Broken on purpose:** the
  one line reverted, **4 of 8 fail**, and the four that stay green are the
  silence assertions, which is the right shape.

  **THE PAGE HALF CANNOT BE PROVED AGAINST PRODUCTION, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
  REASON THIS BOX IS STILL OPEN.** The booking page calls the DEPLOYED
  `calculate-booking`; `supabase functions serve` needs Docker and Docker is
  not on this machine. So the check gained `--stand-in=server`, which adds a
  midday time to the day-only REQUEST so that the live function prices the day
  with its own real `matchPriceRules`, against the real tenant's real rules.
  It proves the PAGE and the live engine's weekday resolution. **It does not
  prove the fixed `whenContextFor`**, which is why the unit test above exists
  and is separate. It cannot silently over-report either: `early-priced`
  asserts the early bar EQUALS the late bar, so a rule matching only because
  of the invented hour turns the run red rather than green.

  | Run, after the fix | Weekend targets | Weekday control |
  |---|---|---|
  | `--stand-in=server` | **PASS 25/25, 195 assertions** · `no day $65 → day $95 → time $95` at all five widths, `Weekend rate · +$30` named on the DAY | `$65 → $65 → $65`, nothing named |
  | Clean, no stand-in | **FAIL, 40 failures** — unchanged, because production has not been published | green |

  **SO THE TICK WAITS ON A PUBLISH RATHER THAN ON WORK, AND THE BOX STAYS OPEN
  UNTIL THE CLEAN RUN PASSES.** ~~BLOCKED~~ — **reframed 2026-09-24: this is
  done on disk and switched off until launch, not blocked.** `DECISIONS.md`
  § *"Publishing is a DEFERRAL, not a blocker"*. `deployed-inventory` now names **8 of 39**
  functions behind this checkout, up from 4, because `_shared/pricing.ts` is
  imported by `calculate-booking`, `create-booking`, `preview-emails`,
  `reschedule-booking` and `update-booking`. That growth is correct and
  expected. **Nothing was deployed.** `FOR-ANDREW.md` carries the row.
  **Done when:** the clean run — no stand-in — passes `early-named`,
  `early-priced`, `early-visible` and `early-painted` at all five widths.

  **AND THE SENTENCE TO READ IF YOU READ NOTHING ELSE HERE, because "blocked
  on deployment" is not something anybody reconstructs six weeks later:**
  **the work is done and a customer cannot see any of it.** Today (measured
  2026-10-06) they are shown $65 on a Sunday and charged $95. After Andrew publishes
  `calculate-booking` they are shown $95 on the Sunday, with the reason
  written next to it, before they choose anything else. Nothing else is

  screen.** `adds-up` was green at every width in every run, before and after:
  the lines sum exactly to the total charged, which is the property 2.2 exists

  | What the label said | What was beside it | Which it really is |
  |---|---|---|
  | `10% off` | **-$5.00 of a $65 job** | **7.69%** |
  | `10% off` | -$15.00 of a $140 job | 10.71% |
  | `15% off` | -$15.00 of a $95 job | 15.79% |
  | `10% off` | -$7.00 of a $65 job, **with no rounding setting at all** | 10.77% |

  **THE ENTRY ABOVE NAMES ONE CAUSE AND THERE ARE TWO — corrected rather than
  quietly fixed.** It says the mismatch needs "a rounding gap to fold into"
  the line. **It does not.** `computeQuote` rounds the discount itself to whole
  dollars first — `Math.round(65 × 0.10)` is 7, and $7 of $65 is 10.77% —
  before any `price_rounding_nearest` is involved. The fold is the second and
  larger cause, not the only one. The last row of the table above is the case
  the old framing said could not happen.

  **DOES THIS AFFECT PROMO CODES? NO, AND HERE IS THE REASON**, because it is
  the first question anyone reading this will ask. The site discount and the
  promo discount are computed side by side in `computeQuote` and the same
  rounding fold touches both — so they do share the arithmetic. But the promo
  line is labelled `Promo SAVE10`: **it states no size, so it has nothing to
  contradict.** Same for the plan line (`{name} · {what}`). Today's rate-limit
  item (14.9) touches `validate-promo-code`, a different program that only
  checks whether a code is real. **They meet at the quote, not in the code.**

  **THE FIX, AND IT IS ONE DECISION MOVED SIX LINES LATER.** The label was
  chosen BEFORE the rounding fold ran, so it described a figure that had not
  finished changing. It is now chosen after, and states a percentage **only
  when that percentage of the job is exactly the figure beside it**. Where it
  cannot, it says `Discount` — **not a new word**: `ManageBookingPage.jsx`
  already names this exact line that way, for the same reason in fewer words
  ("the row cannot say which sale it was"). So the review step and the receipt
  the customer gets afterwards now use the same word for the same line, which
  they did not before. No new string; `es.js` already carries `Descuento`.

  `settings.site_discount_label` on the booking page is always `undefined` and

  sale name was silently shown ours instead, on the one screen where they are

  **WHY THE ROUTE-AROUND IS THE BETTER FIX AND NOT THE LAZIER ONE.** The quote
  is where the value is decided: `calculate-booking` already gates it on

  is switched off. Adding the field to `normalizeSettings` would have put a
  second copy of that value on the page, ungated, arriving by a different road
  from the amount it labels — which is the two-sources-for-one-number shape
  `_shared/pricing.ts` exists to refuse.

  **THE INSTRUMENT: `scripts/discount-label.mjs`.** 15 targets, 90 assertions,
  graded `PASS` by `receipt.mjs`. Six questions per target — `line-present`,
  `adds-up`, `honest`, `form`, `visible`, `painted`.
  **`form` exists because `honest` alone can be satisfied by saying less:**
  deleting every percentage everywhere would pass it, so a second case asserts
  the percentage IS stated where it is true.

  | Run | Result |
  |---|---|
  | **Before the fix** | **FAIL — 10 failures**, `honest` and `form` on the mismatch case at 1920, 1440x900, 768x1024, 392x844 and 320. Committed red on purpose |

  | `adds-up`, same run | green everywhere. The money was never wrong |
  | After the fix | **PASS 15/15** — mismatch reads `«Discount»`, exact still reads `«20% off»` |
  | `--break=canary` | canary 0/5, receipt **rejected** |
  | `--break=paint` | 10 of 10 targets caught |

  **THE `exact` CONTROL WAS 10% IN ITS FIRST DRAFT AND THAT WAS NOT EXACT** —
  10% of $65 is $6.50, which the engine rounds to $7 before any rounding
  setting is involved. A control that is quietly an instance of the fault
  proves nothing. Caught by doing the arithmetic rather than by trusting the
  word "exact" in its own name. It is 20% now: $13.00 of $65.00, to the cent.

  **AND `--break=canary` WAS TOO BLUNT AT FIRST, IN THE SAME WAY.** It skipped
  the whole fixture, so the page had no discount line at all and every
  assertion failed — a sabotage that proves the check can notice an empty page,
  which nobody doubted. It now removes only the detailer's name, turning the
  canary into an ordinary mismatch target the fix handles, so the canary
  observes nothing and the receipt is refused. **A sabotage has to fail for the
  right reason.**

  **SCOPE, AND IT IS IN THE RECEIPT AS WELL AS HERE: THE QUOTE IS A DECLARED
  FIXTURE.** `demo-detail` has **`site_discount_active = false`** — read off
  `business_settings` — so this line does not render there at all. Every target
  injects a site discount, **with `computeQuote`'s own numbers**: the real
  module, imported, asked what a tenant configured that way would be charged.
  What is fabricated is the tenant CONFIGURATION, not the arithmetic.
  **THE LIVE PATH WITH `site_discount_active = true` ON A REAL TENANT WAS NOT
  EXERCISED, at any width, in any run.**

  **THE MEASUREMENT.** `app/src/lib/jobWeather.js:111` geocodes the job's
  address by calling `api.addressSuggest(null, address)` — the **address
  autocomplete** endpoint — to place the weather strip on the job record. That
  endpoint is budgeted as a **typing** allowance:
  `LIMITS.addressPerIp` is **60 an hour per IP**, and its own comment says why
  that number: *"Sixty an hour from one address is a person typing several
  addresses badly; it is not a script, and a debounced field (400ms, four
  characters) spends about six on a real street."* Above it sits
  `addressPerDay`, **2,400 a day, keyed `"all"` — one bucket shared by every
  tenant on the platform.**

  **SO A DETAILER WHO IS NOT TYPING ANYTHING SPENDS A BUDGET SIZED FOR
  CUSTOMERS WHO ARE.** Working through their own job records costs one call
  each. When the hour's sixty are gone, `address-suggest` answers **429**, the
  weather silently stops, and **nothing on the screen says why** — it looks
  like the weather feature is broken rather than rationed.

  **HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the path matters more than the number.**
  `zone-mismatch.mjs` kept reddening on a console line that said only
  *"Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 429"* and
  named nothing. Two runs were spent guessing at buckets — `promo_quote` had
  97 hits and turned out to belong to `platform-billing`, nothing to do with
  it. The instrument was changed to record the PATH of every refused request,
  and the next run named `/functions/v1/address-suggest` immediately, **fired
  by the job record and not by the booking page.**

  **THREE POSSIBLE SHAPES, AND WHICH ONE IS RIGHT IS A JUDGEMENT NOBODY HAS
  MADE.** Not decided here and deliberately not built:
  1. **A cache** — the coordinates for a booking's address do not change, and
     `address_points` already exists for exactly this kind of lookup.
  2. **Its own allowance** — a detailer reading their own records is not a
     stranger typing, and a separate bucket would stop the two competing.
  3. **Nothing at all** — sixty an hour may simply be more than any real
     detailer opens, in which case the only defect is the silent failure.
  **The silent-failure half may be worth separating from the budget half**:
  whatever the limit ends up being, a weather strip that vanishes without a
  word is its own small fault.
  **Done when:** a detailer working through their records does not exhaust an
  allowance meant for customers typing, or — if the limit stays — the screen
  says what happened when it is reached.

  **WHAT WAS BUILT, 2026-09-24 — shapes 1 and the silent-failure half. Shape 2
  was ruled out for this sitting by the manager: its own allowance means
  changing limits inside an edge function, which means a deploy, and deploys
  are Andrew's.**

  **FIRST, THE MEASUREMENT, BECAUSE IT MOVED THE ITEM.** Ten job records at ten
  addresses, opened one after another as a fresh page each time, then the first
  one again — `scripts/job-weather-budget.mjs`, at 1440x900, with the endpoint
  answered in the browser so no Geoapify credit and no hourly bucket was spent.

  | | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | ten records, lookups working | **10 calls** | **10 calls** |
  | reopening the first | **0** | **0** |
  | ten records, lookups REFUSED | **10 calls, every one refused** | **1** |
  | reopening the first, refused | **1 more** | **0** |
  | what the record showed when refused | **nothing at all** | one sentence |

  **SO THE CACHE SHAPE 1 ASKS FOR ALREADY EXISTED, AND THAT IS THE USEFUL
  FINDING.** `dp.weather.points` in `localStorage` has always made a repeat
  address free, and it survives a page load — measured, not read. **One call
  per new address is irreducible from inside `app/src`**: `forecast` takes a
  point and nothing else, and `address-suggest` is the only client-reachable
  way to turn an address into one. Changing that is shape 2, which is a deploy.

  **THE HOLE WAS THE REFUSAL, AND IT HAD NO CEILING.** `pointFor` cached a
  positive *"no such place"* for ever and cached **nothing** for a failure, so
  once the hour's sixty were gone **every further record spent another call
  that could not possibly succeed** — eleven refusals for eleven opens, and a
  detailer who keeps working keeps digging. A 429 is about this browser's hour
  and not about this address, so it is now remembered for **five minutes**, in
  `localStorage` rather than in the module, because the thing it has to survive
  is opening the next record. Five minutes is short enough that the weather
  comes back on its own with nobody reloading anything.

  **AND THE SENTENCE.** *"No weather for this address yet. Address lookups are
  busy right now; it comes back on its own."* — under the address, in the
  record only, never on a scanned row, and **only for a refusal**. Every other
  failure stays silent for the reason `JobWeather.jsx` already gives: a column
  of *unknown* is noise. A refusal is the one failure with something true to
  say about the future. Measured at 6.2:1 on its own ground at 13px; Spanish
  key added in the same edit.

  **PROVED BY BREAKING IT THREE WAYS, each letting through exactly its own
  failure and no other** — `--break=memo` (10 calls after the first refusal),
  `--break=cache` (reopening costs 1), `--break=quiet` (the sentence in the DOM
  and not painted, at all five widths). Two canaries run on every clean pass.
  Receipt: `receipts/job-weather-budget.json`, 7 targets, 14 assertions.

  **AND THE RUN THAT LIED, because it is the part worth reading.** A mid-run
  `refresh-weather` sweep filled in `bookings.weather` on the ten fixture rows,
  so the record painted a stored forecast, never asked anything, and the check
  reported the product broken at five widths. **A scheduled job on the server
  is a second writer on the rows being measured and nothing in the run says it
  arrived** — `docs/gotchas.md` 84. The fixtures are now created `cancelled`,
  which the sweep filters out and the client path does not read, and a forecast
  on a refused record is graded *NOT MEASURED — re-run* rather than as a
  missing sentence.

  **STILL OPEN, AND IT IS ANDREW'S:** the back office still draws on a bucket
  sized for customers typing. Nothing here changes the limit; it changes how
  many times the client asks.

  **WHAT NOBODY HAS PRESSED, SAID PLAINLY RATHER THAN LET PASS — the manager's

  <details><summary>The original finding</summary>

  **Confirmed in source, and it is two pages, not one.**
  `docs/tenant-sites/v-goldenhour-prices.html:1585` and
  `v-goldenhour-work.html:1568` both call
  `document.getElementById("book").scrollIntoView(...)` with no null guard, and

  `/ex1/work` both throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. A1 found
  the prices page; nobody found `/ex1/work`.

  booking anchor by URL instead of scrolling.

  path. An automated check visits every public service CTA across all five

  ── **WHAT THE 2.4 CTA CHECK STILL HAS TO ASSERT — THE ONLY THING LEFT ON
  THIS ITEM. Written to be implemented without asking me.** ─────────────────

  **Whose:** `scripts/`, which is not this session's tree. **Do not extend it
  from here.**

  **THE RULE, in one sentence:** *every control on an example site that offers
  to book a NAMED service must carry that service's identifier, and the
  identifier must match an option the booking widget on the landing page
  actually has.*

  **WHAT TO WALK.** Every page of `ex1`…`ex5` under `app/public/` after
  `build-examples.mjs --dev`. For each page, find every anchor or button whose
  text offers to book something specific — today that is `Book this`,
  `Book <Service Name>` and `Book a <Service Name>`. **A generic `Book`,
  `Book a slot` or `Get a price` is NOT one of these and must not be
  counted**; it offers no service, so there is nothing to carry.

  **WHAT A CORRECT CONTROL LOOKS LIKE. There are three shapes in use and a
  check that knows only one will report working sites as broken — that is not
  hypothetical, it is what happened in this entry:**
  - `data-book="<id>"` — `ex1` (`v-goldenhour-*`) and now `ex3`.
  - `data-pick="<Service Name>"` — `ex4` (`y-kinzie`).
  - `?svc=<id>` already written into the `href` — `ex1`'s cross-page links.
  **Match on the BEHAVIOUR — "does this control name a service" — not on one
  attribute's spelling.**

  **WHAT IT MUST THEN ASSERT, and this is the half that is missing:**
  1. **The identifier resolves.** The value on the control matches the
     `value` of exactly one `input[name="svc"]` in that site's widget —
     **radio OR checkbox**, both are in use.
  2. **The name matches.** The widget option's `<b>` text equals the service
     named on the card it was pressed from.
  3. **The price matches.** The widget option's `<em>` price equals the price
     printed on that card.
  4. **The total follows.** After the press, the `.bk-total` figure equals
     that same price. *(`ex3` does this; the others may not, so a failure
     here is a finding rather than a bug in the check.)*

  **WHAT A WRONG ONE LOOKS LIKE — the four real shapes, all of which existed
  on `ex3` this week:**
  - **No identifier at all.** `<a href="#book">Book this</a>`. The press
    lands on the widget and leaves whatever was `checked` selected. **This is
    the defect the item was opened for**, and the tell is *N controls, 1
    distinct destination*.
  - **An identifier that resolves to nothing.** The control names a service
    the widget does not offer; `pick()` silently matches no option and the
    default stands. **Looks fixed, behaves identically to having no
    identifier.**
  - **A short widget.** The page sells 13 and the widget offers 4, so nine
    cards cannot be satisfied however well the click is carried.
  - **A stale total.** Right service selected, `$500` still printed under it.

  **THE CANARIES TO BREAK IT WITH, so it is certified rather than read** —
  this repo has shipped at least six checks that tested nothing:
  `--break=carry` strips the identifier from one control (expect *no
  identifier*), `--break=resolve` changes one to a service the widget lacks
  (expect *resolves to nothing*), `--break=price` edits one card's price
  (expect *price mismatch*), `--break=total` freezes `.bk-total` (expect
  *stale total*). **Each disabled detector must let through exactly its own
  canary and no other.**

  **TODAY'S EXPECTED RESULT, so a first run has something to be graded
  against:** `ex1` passes, `ex3` passes (13 controls, 13 options, 13 matches),

  ── **AND THE HIT AREA WAS ONE PIXEL SHORT. THE MANAGER FOUND IT BY PRESSING
  IT — 2026-09-21, and this is recorded rather than quietly corrected.**

  **A tick in this round rested on a control that missed a stated absolute,
  the miss was found by somebody opening the screen and probing it, and the
  method that found it was one this session had NAMED as a gap and not yet
  run.** The section above says *"probed with `elementFromPoint` rather than a
  rect"* and reports **44**. The manager's own probe, at `1254x720`, returned
  **43**. **Both numbers were real.**

  **THE ARITHMETIC WAS AGAINST THE WRONG BOX.** `.btn.sm` is `border-box`
  with a 1px border, so its `::after`'s containing block is the **padding
  box — 36px, not 38** — and `inset: -4px 0` computes to **exactly 44px**.
  `getComputedStyle(btn,'::after').height` said `44px` on the nose.

  **EXACTLY 44 ROUNDS UNDER.** The button's top sits at `171.61`, so the
  whole pixel rows it owns are **43, 44 or 45 depending only on where it
  happens to sit.** Scrolling one pixel changes the answer. **A hard absolute
  that is met at some scroll positions and missed at others is missed** — and
  it is why two honest probes disagreed rather than one of us being careless.

  **FIXED ON THE SHARED DECLARATION**, `inset: -4px 0` → `-5px 0`, vertical
  only, horizontal still `0` so the 2026-09-12 *"a sideways box would steal a
  neighbour's press"* decision is untouched. **All 28 `.btn.sm` call sites
  carried the same zero-tolerance 44**; fixing only the button somebody
  pressed would have left 27 one rounding away. `.chip` in the same file
  already used `-5px`, so `.btn.sm` was the outlier rather than the pattern.

  **RE-PROBED, NOT TRUSTED — six scroll positions at each width:**

  | width | press extent, 6 runs | target width | `::after` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **1254 x 720** | **47, 47, 47, 47, 47, 47** | 963px | 46px |
  | **320 x 844** | **47, 47, 47, 47, 47, 47** | 284px | 46px |

  **Never below 44 at either**, nearest interactive neighbour still **29px**
  away at 320, so nothing steals a press. Build clean, four suites, label-guard
  45/45, admin-insight 65/65, customer-export 18/18.

  **THREE MORE CONTROLS ARE IN THE IDENTICAL POSITION — read off the CSS, not
  pressed, so named rather than changed:**

  | control | min-height | border | padding box | inset | target |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `.btn.sm` | 38 | 1px | 36 | **−5** | **46** ✔ fixed |
  | `.chip` | 36 | 1px | 34 | −5 | **44** — zero tolerance |
  | `.choice` | 38 | 1px | 36 | −4 | **44** — zero tolerance |
  | `.segmented button` | 36 | 0 | 36 | −4 | **44** — zero tolerance |

  **Three controls sitting exactly on the absolute, each one rounding away
  from missing it.** Not touched: they are on screens this session did not
  press, and the last thing this entry needs is a fourth number changed on
  arithmetic alone.

  **AND IT IS THE CLEANEST ARGUMENT FOR 4.5 THERE IS.** The suites do not
  reach the back office — and neither did anything else until a person opened

  ── **THE THREE WERE PRESSED — 2026-09-21. All three pass, all three pass
  with nothing in hand, and the change that fixed `.btn.sm` put `.btn.sm`
  itself at 43 on a screen it never opened.**

  **Measured with `elementFromPoint`, every control walked row by row, at
  320x844 AND 1254x720, each one swept through a full pixel of sub-pixel
  offset** (`translateY` 0 → 0.9 — a whole-pixel scroll leaves the offset
  identical and the rounding under test never moves, which is why the first
  three runs of this probe saw no variation at all).

  | control | `::after` computes | pressed, 320 | pressed, 1254 | vertical slack | sideways |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `.chip` | **44px** | **44–45** | **44–45** | **2px** (Hours, wrapped) | 4px dead |
  | `.choice` | **44px** | **45** | **45** | **2px** (Booking rules, Promos) | 4px dead |
  | `.segmented button` | **44px** (55.19 where it wraps its label at 320) | **45** / 56–57 | **45** | no wrapped pair on any screen reached | 1px dead |
  | `.btn.sm` | 46px | **43 on Hours**, 46–47 elsewhere | 46–47 | **0px** (Hours) | — |

  **Coverage, because a skipped control reads exactly like a passing one:**
  41/41 `.choice` on Booking rules, 6/6 on Promos, 11/11 `.segmented button`
  on Booking rules, 7/7 `.chip` on Hours, 10/10 `.btn.sm` on Hours, at both
  widths — **0 unmeasured.** The first three runs measured only 12 of the 41
  `.choice`, and said nothing: **29 of them sit inside two CLOSED
  `<details class="foldrow">`, which still report full-size rects for their
  children** (`docs/gotchas.md`). The probe now opens every `<details>` first.

  **THE ARITHMETIC IN THE TABLE ABOVE IS EXACTLY RIGHT AND THE CONCLUSION
  DRAWN FROM IT IS NOT.** *"Exactly 44 rounds under … 43, 44 or 45 depending
  only on where it happens to sit"* — **43 is not reachable.** A band of
  height 44.0 starting at a fractional `y` contains `floor(a+44) − ceil(a) +
  1` whole pixel rows, which is **44 when `a` is fractional and 45 when it is
  whole. Never 43.** Tested rather than argued: a synthetic control whose
  `::after` computes to exactly 44px, dropped into the live page and probed by
  the same code, read **44,45,45,45,45,45,45,45,45,45** — and a known 46px one
  read **46,47,…** — at device scale factors **1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2**.
  Fifty readings, no 43.

  **So the manager's 43 was real and its cause is NOT the inset.** The
  candidate that fits is their own pane: it pins its layout viewport at 1414
  and displays it smaller, and a scaled ancestor paints a 44px band at 43.x.
  **Unproven — it is their apparatus, which this session cannot reach.** It
  changes nothing about the fix; it changes what the next session should
  believe about the mechanism.

  **AND THE FIX FOR `.btn.sm` BROKE `.btn.sm`.** Growing that band from 44 to
  46 helped every call site with nothing above or below it, and broke the one
  place three of them **wrap**. On **Hours at 320**, "All days", "Weekdays"
  and "Weekends" sit in a `.row.wrap` that goes to two lines on a phone;
  `.row`'s gap is `--sp-2` = 6px, so the pitch is 38 + 6 = **44**, which a
  44px band tiled exactly and a 46px band cannot. The two bands **overlapped
  by 2px**, the lower button won the contested rows, and **"All days"
  measured 44, 44, 43, 43** across a pixel of offset while "Weekends" read a
  full 46–47. **That is trap (n) — a small target traded for a WRONG one.**
  **Fixed** on the shared declaration, third instance of the pattern `.chip`
  and `.choice` already carry: `.btn.sm { margin-block: 1px }` makes the pitch
  38 + 1 + 1 + 6 = **46**, which the 46px band tiles exactly. **Re-probed, not
  trusted:** "All days" now reads **45–46** at every offset, and a full
  re-sweep of all four controls across 8 screens × 2 widths returns **0 under
  44**.

  **THE PITCH WAS THE RECORDED SUSPICION AND IT IS INNOCENT. Cleared by
  measurement, not by arithmetic, and the arithmetic agrees.** `.choice`'s
  pressable band is **44px** on a **46px** pitch — `.choice` is `border-box`
  with a 1px border, so the `::after`'s containing block is the 36px PADDING
  box and `inset: -4px 0` computes to 44, which the correction already sitting
  beside `.choice::after` in `theme.css` records. That is **2px of slack
  between wrapped rows, not 2px of overlap.** And the row-by-row walk settles
  it without needing the arithmetic at all: **the lost rows are a contiguous
  run at the BOTTOM of the chip owned by an ANCESTOR**, never an alternating
  pattern owned by the chip next door. A gap would have been the wrong change
  in the wrong place, which is the whole reason it was measured first.

  **WHAT WAS ACTUALLY EATING THE FOUR ROWS — the second suspicion on the list,
  "a clip or `overflow` on the settings container at desk widths".** At 1440
  and 1920 the settings column stops at the screen's height and **scrolls
  inside itself** (`.settings-col > .settings-body`, `theme.css:1686`). Its
  clip edge at 1440x900 is y **856**; `scrollIntoView({block:"end"})` plus
  focus parks the chip's box bottom at **855.69**, flush against it, and the
  4px of `::after` that reaches past the box lands **outside the scroller and
  is clipped**. `elementFromPoint` then names `.app-main` — what is visible
  below the clip edge — which is exactly what the original measurement
  reported. At 320, 392 and 768 the same screen is a PAGE, the document is the
  scroller, and 2.32's `html:has(.tabbar)` rule already reserves the overhang:
  45px, unchanged.

  **SO 2.32's FIX COULD NOT HAVE HELPED, AND THE REASON IS ONE WORD.** That
  rule is on `html`. `scroll-padding-bottom` is a property of **the scroller
  being scrolled**, and at these widths the scroller is not the document.

  **THE FIX — one declaration, three selectors, `theme.css` beside 2.32's:**
  `.settings-col > .settings-body, .record > .record-body, .sheet-body
  { scroll-padding-bottom: var(--hit-overhang); }`. It reserves the overhang
  and nothing else; it is not clearance for a bar, because there is no bar
  here.

  **ALL THREE SCROLLERS, AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** Only the
  settings body had a control parked flush the night this was found. The check
  asks the **scrollers** as well as the controls, and it found the record body
  and the sheet body reserving **nothing at all** against a real 4px overhang —
  the same clip, one control away from the same loss. One rule, not three call
  sites, for the reason the `.choice` note gives.

  | scrollers reserving less than the overhang | **7 of 7** | **0 of 7** |

  this function running this checkout"* — a different question. A function can
  match the checkout while an item's claim about it is months out of date, and
  it can differ for a reason that has nothing to do with the item. Nothing
  reads an item's claim at all.

  **THE ASK, AND IT IS SMALLER THAN A CHECK: a claim about something OUTSIDE
  the repo carries the date it was measured.** "It is not live" is not a fact
  about this repository; it is a reading taken at a moment, of a system that
  changes without a commit. Written undated it reads as permanent. Written
  **"not live — measured 2026-09-21"** it tells a reader in one glance how much
  to trust it, and 2.8's two-day gap becomes visible the moment anyone looks.
  The same applies to anything resting on a deployed bundle, a live setting, a
  third-party dashboard or a database column.

  **SHAPES, NOT A CHOICE:**
  1. **A convention only** — every such claim carries its date, enforced by
     nothing, which is how most of this repo's rules already work.
  2. **A check that re-asks** — reads the dated claims out of `ROADMAP.md` and
     re-measures the ones it can, going red when a claim and the world
     disagree.
  3. **A staleness budget** — a dated claim older than N days reports as
     unproven rather than as true, the same way `receipt.mjs` already grades a
     receipt written at an older commit.
  **Done when:** no open item's blocker can be two days out of date without a
  reader being able to see how old the claim is.
  **The three entries written tonight already carry their dates**, which is
  the convention being proposed, applied once.

  ### ASKED AGAIN 2026-09-25 EXPECTING STALENESS. IT WAS STALE THE OTHER WAY: THE FAULT WAS LIVE.

  **EVERYTHING ABOVE THIS LINE IS TRUE OF THE DEMO'S OWN STRINGS AND WAS NEVER
  TRUE OF A TENANT'S.** Andrew, 2026-09-25: *"the footer's height is
  content-driven and its widest line is text the DETAILER typed — so a tenant
  with a longer service name is the case that breaks it, not the demo's."*
  He was right, and nothing here had ever run that case.

  **2.15 DELETED A LITERAL AND A SECOND COPY OF IT SURVIVED ONE PROPERTY
  ALONG.** `.bk-wrap`'s 104px reserve went and the bar became `sticky`. But
  `booking.css`'s **`--bk-bar-h: 73px`** stayed, and 8.5a's
  `scroll-padding-bottom: calc(var(--bk-bar-h) + 12px + var(--safe-b))` is what
  decides where the browser may park a control that takes focus.

  **THE LITERAL CARRIED A MEASUREMENT THAT USED THE WRONG STRING, AND SAID SO
  IN ITS OWN COMMENT.** *"The height is set by the Continue button, not by the
  text"*, so a wrapped eyebrow reaches *"76px and no further"* — proved by
  forcing a long **total** into the bar at 320, where it grew 3px. **A total is
  a formatted number. The eyebrow's other half is `plan_name`, free text, and
  `Plans.jsx` allows 60 characters of it.** A measurement that names its own
  input is still wrong if the input is not the one that varies.

  | 320x844, 59-character plan name | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | damage step, bar height | **112px** | 112px |
  | … footer covers | **21px of Light, Moderate, Heavy, Extreme** | **nothing** |
  | … a real press on «Extreme» | **landed on the footer** | lands on «Extreme» |
  | review step, bar height | **184px** | 184px |
  | … worst reachable | **10px of 44** | **44px** |
  | … a real press | **lost to the footer** | lands |

  **FIXED WITH 2.15's OWN MOVE, WHERE THE NUMBER SURVIVED: stop asserting the
  height, measure it.** A callback ref on `.bk-bar` writes its measured height
  to `--bk-bar-h` on `documentElement` — on `html`, because the rule computes
  there and a property on `.bk` is invisible to it, which is the defect
  `booking.css` spends thirty lines on. The literal stays as the first-paint
  fallback. **The 12px is untouched**; this item had already recorded 8.5a's
  step as not its to spend, and that still holds — only the number it is added
  to has changed.

  **WHY A ResizeObserver IS RIGHT HERE HAVING BEEN WRONG ABOVE.** The one this
  item threw away was for `.bk-wrap`'s padding, rejected because it preserved
  the fragile *"the reserve must equal the height"* relationship that `sticky`
  deletes outright. **`scroll-padding-bottom` cannot be expressed relationally
  in CSS at all**, so here that relationship is not fragile, it is the
  definition.

  **`bk-bar-clearance.mjs` NOW ASKS THE QUESTION THAT CAUGHT IT.** A second
  sweep at the 60-character ceiling — the string put on the wire, **nothing
  written to `plans`** — a `pressed` question that sends a real pointer and
  reads who the browser handed it to, and a second canary: the same long name
  against the old reserve. **36 targets to 72, 168 assertions to 420, both
  canaries bite.**

  **60 IS THE CEILING AND IT IS THE ONLY ENFORCEMENT ANYWHERE.** `maxLength` on
  one React input. `plans.name` is bare `text` with no check constraint and no
  edge function in the write path, so PostgREST or an import can exceed it —
  and the same repo does bound `vehicle_size` and the payment handles.
  **Recorded, not fixed: a constraint on live data is a migration, and that is
  Andrew's.**

  **TWO MISTAKES OF MINE, BOTH CAUGHT BY THE CHECK AND NEITHER BY ME.** The
  intercept first set `body.plan_name` where the page reads
  `body.quote.plan_name`, so the new sweep ran five widths against the demo's
  own 21-character name and **printed green over a case it had not tested** —
  the tell was bar heights byte-identical to the short sweep. And the first fix
  used `useRef` + `useEffect([])`; **there is no bar on mount**, so it took its
  early return and never ran again, writing the property zero times while the
  page looked perfect and nothing errored.

  **THE BOX STAYS OPEN AND THE REASON HAS NOT CHANGED.** The on-screen keyboard
  is still unmeasured and still unmeasurable here; Andrew's 2026-09-20 ruling
  governs. What moved is that the clearance half is now true of a string a
  detailer can actually type, which it was not yesterday.

  **AND WHAT THE 320 EVIDENCE ACTUALLY IS, IN ANDREW'S OWN WORDS RATHER THAN AS
  A CAVEAT — 2026-09-25.** He opened the booking page in his own browser at the
  width Andrew's window actually is and read it: it loads, the last service

  has 288.** A seven-column month cannot carry a 44px-wide target on the
  narrowest phone this product supports, whatever the spacing is. Anything
  that claims otherwise has changed the layout, not the spacing.

- [x] **DONE 2026-09-20 — the booking column had been rendering at under
  half its own declared width, on every step; the calendar's day cells are
  52 by 52 now, square, at desktop.** Found by the other session's
  booking-steps triage, 2026-09-20, root-caused on a fresh load rather than
  a resize. **The before number, so the size of this is visible without
  re-measuring anything: `.bk-wrap` rendered at 316.9px against its own
  declared `max-width` of 632px.**
  **THE CAUSE.** `.bk-wrap` (`app/src/book/booking.css`) is a flex child of
  `.bk`, which is `display: flex; flex-direction: column`. `margin: 0 auto`
  on a flex item puts AUTO margins on its CROSS axis (width, in a
  column-direction parent) — and per the flex spec, cross-axis auto margins
  absorb the leftover space and override `align-items: stretch` for that
  one item. With no `width` declared, `.bk-wrap` never stretched toward the
  `max-width` it was supposed to be centred WITHIN; it shrank to its
  content's width instead, and the margin only centred that narrow box.
  Confirmed structurally before fixing anything: `.bk-header` and
  `.bk-center`, the other two direct children of `.bk`, do not carry
  `margin: 0 auto` on themselves and do not have this fault — the max-width
  pairing that collapses lives one level deeper on `.bk-header .inner`, a
  plain block rather than a flex item, where the ordinary CSS centring rule
  applies without a flex parent's cross-axis override.
  **THE CALENDAR'S CELLS ARE DOWNSTREAM, NOT A SECOND FAULT — checked, not
  assumed.** `.bk-cal { grid-template-columns: repeat(7, 1fr) }`: proportional
  columns, no fixed pixel width anywhere in the cell's own rule. A cell's
  size is entirely a function of `.bk-wrap`'s width, which is why the file's
  own comment already expects 47px on a 360px phone column and the design
  absolute is 44px, while the measured width gave 36.4px — one fault seen
  twice, which is why the fix is the wrap, not the cell.
  **THE FIX, AND IT IS A FIX RATHER THAN A REDESIGN, SAID IN THOSE WORDS ON
  PURPOSE.** `width: 100%;` added to `.bk-wrap`, one line, restoring the
  width the stylesheet has always declared and never reached — the
  `max-width` and the `margin: 0 auto` were always correct; nothing here
  was designed narrow. **But it is not a one-screen change and should not be
  waved through as one:** `.bk-wrap` is shared by all five booking-side
  pages (`BookingPage.jsx` — all seven steps, `BookingConfirmed.jsx`,
  `ManageBookingPage.jsx`, `PlanMemberPage.jsx`, `PlansPage.jsx`), so this
  visibly widens every one of them; step 1 alone moves from 469px to 632px.
  That is why this is held for a press at four widths rather than accepted
  on the diff.
  **SPANISH, CHECKED BEFORE CALLING THIS DONE, EVEN THOUGH THE CHANGE IS
  CSS.** Swept `booking.css` for anything sized to the narrow, buggy
  measurement — no literal `316`/`317` anywhere, and every `white-space:
  nowrap` on the five steps sits on content that either shrinks the risk
  when the column widens (a mono price, a short pill, a badge) or already
  wraps its container (`.bk-plan-chips { flex-wrap: wrap }`) rather than
  overflowing. **This is a static check, not a rendered one** — it rules out
  a value hard-coded to the broken width, it does not prove Spanish copy
  looks right at 632px, which the press below still has to do.
  **ONE THING NOT TO DO, AND IT IS NAMED HERE SO NOBODY REACHES FOR IT ON A
  QUIET NIGHT — the other session's find, kept in its own words because the
  reason is the useful part.** Do not fix the day cells with the `::after`
  negative-inset trick this repo uses elsewhere for a small, isolated mark.
  Calendar cells sit adjacent with only a 5px gap; a negative inset large
  enough to reach a 44px target would extend roughly 4px into each
  neighbour, so the 21st and 22nd of the month would steal each other's
  presses and `elementFromPoint` would return the wrong date along the edge
  of every cell. On a date picker that trades a small target for a WRONG
  one, and the wrong answer here is a booking made on the wrong day. The
  grid's width is the fix; the cell was never the fault.
  **FOUR NUMBERS DECIDE WHETHER THIS WORKED, NOT WHAT THE SCREEN LOOKS
  LIKE, AND ALL FOUR ARE THE OTHER SESSION'S TO RE-MEASURE:** `.bk-wrap` at
  632px on a fresh load (not a resize); the calendar's day cells clearing
  44px; the booking-steps gate's roughly seventy tap-target findings going

  A fix that moves the number but leaves any of these four where they were

  **Built code-only, held for the press — the other session has the browser

  against the 316.9 it was. Walked five steps as a customer — service,

  **THE 52 IS THE BETTER HALF OF THE STORY, SO IT LEADS THIS ENTRY RATHER

  happened at desktop is a DIFFERENT rule, `.bk-cal .cell`'s `max-height:

  **THE SECOND-INSTANCE SWEEP OF `booking.css`, WRITTEN DOWN SO THE NEXT

## Wave 3 — Communication proof

"Sent" is not "delivered". Today the product proves only that a send was
requested.

- [ ] **3.1 — The owner cannot tell whether emails arrived.**
  The dashboard says "Reminder sent to customer"; the back office says Resend
  delivery/bounce tracking is "confirmed possible" and not wired.
  **Fix:** store and display Resend events for `sent`, `delivered`,
  `delivery_delayed`, `bounced`, `failed`, `suppressed` and `complained`, each
  linked to message, booking, detailer and recipient. Alert on permanent
  failure. Resend documents exactly these event types for webhooks.
  **Done when:** a deliberately bounced test message appears in the back office
  with a next action, and a delivered one is visibly different from "sent".
  *A1 P0-04, § 9*
  **HALF DONE 2026-09-16 by 14.3, and the half that is left is small.** The
  events are stored and displayed: a delivered message is now visibly different
  from one merely sent (*"Delivered"* with a tick, against *"On its way"*), a
  deliberately bounced message reads *"Bounced"* in red with the provider's own
  reason, and a permanent failure raises the address banner on the customer.
  **What 3.1 still asks for that 14.3 did not build:** the same list in the
  **back office** rather than only on the client record, and the link to the
  BOOKING (the row carries business, customer, address and subject — not the
  booking id, because the relay is never told which booking it is sending
  about). `delivery_delayed` and `suppressed` are deliberately not modelled;
  `supabase/functions/resend-webhook/index.ts` says why.

  ***SERVER HALF BUILT 2026-10-06 — THE BOOKING ID NOW REACHES THE ROW, AND
  NOTHING IS DEPLOYED OR APPLIED.*** Both of those are Andrew's and both are
  switches in `FOR-ANDREW.md`.

  **What was wrong, in one sentence:** every booking sender had the booking in
  hand while it composed the mail, and threw the id away at the relay boundary
  because `sendTenantEmail` had nowhere to put it.

  **The three hops, each of which could drop it with no symptom at all:**

  | hop | file | what it now does |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | `supabase/functions/_shared/email.ts` | `sendTenantEmail` takes `bookingId` and forwards it as `booking_id` |
  | 2 | `supabase/functions/send-email/index.ts` | reads `booking_id` off the request into one `SendContext`, built once |
  | 3 | the same file's `record()` | writes `booking_id` on the `email_sends` row |
  | — | `supabase/migrations/20261006010000_an_email_row_knows_its_booking.sql` | adds the column, `on delete set null`, with a partial index for the back-office query |

  **15 of the 28 `sendTenantEmail` call sites now pass a booking id; the other
  13 are about no booking and a null is correct for them** — an invite, a
  campaign to a whole list, a plan link, platform billing, the dead man's
  switch, and `send-owner-reminders`' maintenance nudge, which is about a due
  date on a vehicle rather than an appointment.

  **`tests/email-row-knows-its-booking.test.mjs` is the guard, and it
  DISCOVERS the senders rather than listing them** — `_shared/email.ts` carries
  that same warning about `extraVehiclesFor` because a hand-written caller list
  here was already short by one. The no-booking senders are declared BY NAME,
  so one leaving is ordinary work and **one arriving uninvited is the finding**.
  Broken on purpose three ways, each caught by the section aimed at it: the
  insert line removed (hop 3), the relay forward removed (hop 1), and the
  argument removed at one real call site (section 5 named the file and line).

  ---

  ### THE `app/src` HALF — what Lane A renders, so it can start without asking

  **The data is there after the migration runs. Nothing below needs another
  server change**, and if something seems to, say so rather than adding one.

  ***THE “WHERE” BELOW WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED, 2026-10-06, BEFORE LANE A
  BUILT IT.*** The first version named `AdminPage.jsx` AND said a detailer's
  session reads the rows through the `for select` policy AND linked to
  `/admin/job/:id`. **Those three cannot all be true**, the manager caught it,
  and the routes settle it:

  | | the screen | the route | how it reads the rows |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **a DETAILER** | their own job record and client record | `/job/:id`, `/app/:tab` | their session, through `email_sends`' existing `for select` policy scoped by `current_business_ids()` |
  | **ANDREW** | the platform back office | `/admin` | **the `platform-admin` edge function under the service role** |

  **`/admin` IS ANDREW'S ALONE AND NO DETAILER SEES IT** — 9.12 describes it as
  a list OF detailers (*“detailer, status, setup, last booking, earned,
  customers”*), `main.jsx:126` comments that its whole point is being outside
  the tree a detailer opens, and `AdminPage.jsx:22` says **every byte still
  comes from the `platform-admin` edge function**.

  **SO THE DATA PATH DEPENDS ON WHICH SCREEN, AND GETTING IT WRONG RETURNS AN
  EMPTY LIST THAT LOOKS CORRECT.** `email_sends`' policy scopes to
  `current_business_ids()`, and **Andrew is not a member of each detailer's
  business** — so a browser query from `/admin` returns zero rows with no
  error. It must be a new action on `platform-admin`, the way every other
  figure on that screen already is.

  **WHICH ONE DOES 3.1 ASK FOR? ANDREW'S.** Its Fix says the list is linked to
  *“message, booking, detailer and recipient”* — **a detailer does not need a
  link to themselves**, so the reader is one level up. And its half-done note
  asks for *“the same list in the back office rather than only on the client
  record”*: the client record is the detailer's and already exists.

  **WHAT LANE A SHOULD BUILD, THEN:** the list on `/admin`, fed by a new
  `platform-admin` action. **The detailer-side view is already built and is not
  this item.** If the detailer's own business-wide list is wanted later, that is
  a separate item and a separate data path.


  **WHAT ONE ROW SHOWS.** `email_sends` columns, all already readable by a
  detailer's session through the existing `for select` policy:

  | column | how it draws |
  |---|---|
  | `subject` | the handle a person recognises the message by — this is the label, not a `kind` lookup |
  | `to_email` | the recipient, under the subject |
  | `status` | the seven states, and **`sent` and `delivered` must look different** — that is 3.1's own Done-when. The existing words are *"On its way"* and *"Delivered"* with a tick, and `bounced` is red with `detail` beneath it. **Reuse those exact words**; a second vocabulary for the same column is how two screens disagree |
  | `detail` | the provider's own reason, one line, only on a bad outcome. It is null for `delivered` on purpose |
  | `sent_at` | when it was handed over, newest first |
  | **`booking_id`** | **the new one — links to the job record at `/admin/job/:id`** |

  **THE THREE LINKS 3.1 ASKS FOR, and the third is the new one:**
  **recipient** → the customer record via `customer_id`; **detailer** → the
  business, which in the back office is the row you are already inside;
  **booking** → `/admin/job/<booking_id>`, the same path
  `send-owner-reminders` already uses.

  **A NULL `booking_id` IS NOT AN ERROR AND MUST NOT RENDER AS ONE.** Campaign
  mail, invites, plan links and platform mail are correctly null. Draw no link
  and no placeholder — **not a greyed-out "no booking" chip**, which invites a
  detailer to wonder what went wrong. The absence is the answer.

  **THE ALERT 3.1 ASKS FOR IS ALREADY BUILT AND MUST NOT BE BUILT TWICE.**
  *"Alert on permanent failure"* is `customers.email_failed_at`, which the
  webhook stamps and `Clients.jsx` already draws as *"This address bounced"*.
  The back-office list needs no second alerting mechanism — it needs the bounced
  rows to be **findable**, which is a filter or a sort, not a notification.

  **WHAT FAILING LOOKS LIKE, so it is not reported as done:** a list that shows
  `sent` and `delivered` with the same words (3.1's Done-when fails on exactly
  that), a booking link drawn for a null id, or a list that reads the client
  record's query and is therefore scoped to one customer — the whole point is

  when it is made, one the day before the appointment — each of which (a) a
  detailer can switch off independently, (b) leaves a delivery row in this
  product's own tables, and (c) stops being sent when its switch is off.** And
  **a customer's reply CHANGES THE BOOKING and not merely a log** — on a
  **request-mode** booking, *"Reply C to confirm"* moves it to the state
  `respond-to-booking` would have set, and the row recording the reply is the
  evidence rather than the deliverable. **On a reserve-mode booking there is
  nothing to confirm, so the confirmation text does not offer a reply at all** —
  and that, not a silent pass, is what "done" looks like there.
  ***SECOND COLD READ, 2026-10-02: the first repair said the reply "moves the
  booking into the state the detailer would otherwise have had to set by hand"
  and named neither the state nor the mode.*** `booking_mode` is `request` or
  `reserve` (`core.js`, falling back to `reserve`), and **in reserve mode nothing
  needs confirming** — so the clause was unexecutable on half the product and a
  stranger would have had to ask which half.

  2026-10-02 caught it — `docs/open-items-read-as-a-stranger-2026-09-25.md` batch
  12. **A reply logged and acted on by nobody would have passed**, while the Fix
  says *confirm*. Same fault this session has recorded against itself before: a
  fold that keeps the mechanism and drops the thing that made it matter.)*
  **And the day-before text is sent on the detailer's own existing
  `reminder_lead_minutes`, not on a time invented here** — the column exists;
  "the day before" names no hour and two people would pick two.
  **The delivery row is the shape `email_sends` already has for email** — one row
  per attempted send, carrying what became of it — named as the model rather than
  inventing a table here, because the SMS one does not exist yet and 0.13 is
  where it gets built.
  **What failing looks like:** a text that arrives and leaves no row — the shape
  every email fault in this repo has had — or **a switch that removes the message
  from the screen while the send still happens**, which reads as working from
  both ends.
  **HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM 0.13, so neither is closed by the other:** 0.13 is the
  **pipe** — one message, any message, with a receipt coming back through the
  webhook. **3.3 is the two product messages, their switches and the reply.**
  0.13 can be finished while 3.3 is untouched; 3.3 cannot start until it is.
  *A2 3.1, A2 Part 8 item 1 — A2 calls this the single biggest cut to no-shows*

  ### FRONT HALF DONE 2026-09-21 — the classification, on the source.
  ### THE BACK HALF — rendering and end-to-end sending — IS NOT DONE.

  **The question this answers, and it had never been asked.** Andrew's ruling at
  the time, **reversed by him on 2026-09-21 and no longer binding — live version
  in `docs/MANAGER-CLOSE-2026-09-21.md` § 2**: *no marketing email, ever. Email
  is receipts, reminders and alerts; anything that sells goes by text.*
  **The classification below is unaffected and is still worth having** — it
  records which of the four kinds each template IS, which is a fact about the
  templates rather than about the rule. What expired is the conclusion that a
  marketing template must not exist. Every template was previously read for
  whether it is CLEAR. None was read for **which of those four it is**. Nothing
  was rendered and nothing was sent this round; nothing was fixed, by
  instruction.

  **HOW EACH CLASSIFICATION WAS ESTABLISHED — evidence, not the function's
  name.** Four tests, applied to every template: (a) **what the button asks
  the reader to do**, which is the sharpest single signal — every call-to-action
  in the file was listed and read together; (b) **whether the subject is a
  booking that already exists**, or a new one being solicited; (c) **whether it
  carries a CAN-SPAM legal footer** (`legal:` passed to `shell`), which is the
  product's own declaration of whether it thinks a mail is marketing; (d) **the
  trigger function and its gate**, read in the sender rather than assumed from
  the template.

  | # | Template | Trigger → who receives it | Class | Evidence |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | `customerConfirmationEmail` | `create-booking`, `accept-quote` → customer | **Receipt** | "View your booking" — a booking that now exists |
  | 2 | `invoiceEmail` | `send-invoice` → customer | **Receipt** | money owed or paid for work done; no CTA to buy |
  | 3 | `requestDecisionEmail` · accepted / declined | `respond-to-booking` → customer | **Receipt** | the answer to a request they made |
  | 4 | `requestDecisionEmail` · quote | `respond-to-booking` → customer | **Receipt** | "See it and say yes" — a price for a job THEY asked for. A quote is solicited, so it is not a sale |
  | 5 | `customerReminderEmail` | `send-owner-reminders` sweep → customer | **Reminder** | "View or change your booking" — an appointment already agreed |
  | 6 | `ownerNewBookingEmail` | `create-booking`, `accept-quote` → detailer | **Alert** | "Open the job" — something needs attention |
  | 7 | `ownerNewBookingEmail` reused | `send-owner-reminders` evening-before → detailer | **Reminder** | same template, subject swapped; finding 6 above |
  | 8 | `staleRequestEmail` | `send-owner-reminders` → detailer | **Alert** | "Answer this request" — an unanswered request |
  | 9 | `cancellationEmail` | `cancel-booking`, `update-booking` → both | **Alert** | a state change on an existing booking |
  | 10 | `rescheduleEmail` | `reschedule-booking`, `update-booking` → both | **Alert** | as above |
  | 11 | `planCancelledEmail` | `plan-link` → customer | **Alert** | a plan they held has ended |
  | 12 | `planLinkEmail` | `plan-link` → customer | **Receipt** | "Open your plan" — sent AFTER sign-up, not to solicit one |
  | 13 | `inviteEmail` | `invite-user`, `platform-admin` → staff | **Alert** | "Set up your account" — an account action |
  | 14 | `billingEmail` | `stripe-webhook` → detailer | **Alert** | "Update your card" / "Put your page back online" |
  | 15 | `platformAlertEmail` | `create-business`, `watch-jobs` → platform owner | **Alert** | internal, to Andrew |
  | 16 | `followupEmail` | `send-invoice`, gated `email_customer_followup` → customer | **Neither — see D** | asks for a Google/Yelp review |
